answer: Practically, the chain should require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because copper only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, prism is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any summit approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
